feature: An agent reaches the running app, reads the open document and sees it
summary: An agent session (Claude Code) with the Photonz MCP server can list the documents open in Photonz, open a file or a History item, read the front document as structured data, see it as a picture, a video frame or a contact sheet, and undo or redo, all in the app you have open.
setup: Photonz Probe (or Dev, once rebuilt), release Next, no switch changed: the new switch 'Agents can work in Photonz' is on by default in Next. Install the server once with Scripts/install-mcp.sh (Scripts/install-mcp.sh --probe for the probe), then start a new Claude Code session.

try.do: Run Scripts/install-mcp.sh in the repo, then start a new Claude Code session.
Open a recording in Photonz, then ask the session: what is open in Photonz, and show me the frame 10 seconds in.
try.shotNote: This is the picture the agent was handed (the video frame tool's PNG), not a capture of the window: the feature has nothing on screen of its own.

try.do: Ask: show me a contact sheet of the whole video.
try.shotNote: The contact sheet tool's PNG, as the agent sees it.

try.do: Draw a rectangle on a screenshot by hand, then ask the session to undo the last step. The rectangle goes; ask it to redo and it comes back.
Ask: open the newest item in my History and tell me what is in it.
Quit Photonz and ask again what is open: the server starts Photonz in the background and answers.

evaluate: Is one command from the repo the install you want for now, or should the server ship inside the app so a release user needs no repo?
When an agent opens a document, Photonz comes to the front with it, as if you had opened it. Is that right, or should agent work stay behind your current app?
Should agents be able to reach Photonz by default in Next (they can now), or only after you switch it on?
Is a 1024 pixel picture the right default for what the agent sees, given that bigger costs the session more?
rough: No mock covers this surface: it has no window of its own, so the pictures here are what the agent is handed, not window captures.

A recording handed to Photonz as it starts never opens (a picture does), so 'the probe open on a recording' was set up by opening it after launch. Filed as a-recording-handed-to-photonz-as-it-starts-opens.

The frame shown for exactly 10.000 s is stamped 9.967 s, one frame early; the canvas and export show the same frame. The agent spotted it on its own. Filed as the-frame-shown-at-a-whole-second-is-the-one-tha.
This slice has no editing tools yet, so undo was checked on a rectangle a scripted walk drew, then undone and redone through the server.
The very first session on a Mac, before Photonz has ever run with this switch, starts Photonz to learn its tool list; after that a session starts it only when a tool is called.
The install needs this repo and builds a small helper program the first time (about 4 seconds).
